query: As of early July 2026, what percentage of Russia's national oil-refining capacity is offline/disabled due to Ukrainian drone strikes?
answer:
Research complete. Summary of what I found:

**The direct answer to "as of early July 2026":** **42.7% (42.74%)** — announced by Ukraine's General Staff on 4 July 2026, and the figure Kyiv Post explicitly datelines "as of early July 2026." It was carried by Kyiv Post, Euromaidan Press, UATV, UNN, United24, Ukranews, and Express Tribune.

**But that's an official Ukrainian military claim, and independent analysts sat lower and wider:**
- FT (8–9 Jul), citing analysts: **20–40%**
- Energy Intelligence (9 Jul): "nearly half," **>3.1 mb/d** of 6.6 mb/d (~47%)
- OIES (Jul): **~one-third** offline at a single point in time as of mid-June
- Wood Mackenzie: **2.7 mb/d** CDU outages in July (~41–43%)
- Kpler (14 Jul): **58%** downtime+attacked — but only **1.5–2.0 mb/d effectively offline** (~20–27%)
- Honchar (30 Jun): **50%**; IEA/Reuters sources: **33–40%**

**The key methodological finding** is that these aren't really contradictory — they measure five different things: cumulative capacity attacked (OIES: 81%, i.e. 24 of 34 refineries covering 5.1 mb/d), nameplate capacity of plants disabled, capacity offline at a point in time, downtime including scheduled maintenance, and output shortfall. The denominator also varies (OIES 6.27 mb/d, EI 6.6 mb/d, Kpler's arithmetic implies ~7.4 mb/d).

**Hardest evidence is throughput**, which is less contestable: runs fell from ~4.6 mb/d in March to **3.7–4.1 mb/d in June** (lowest in 21 years) and ~3.8–3.9 mb/d in mid-July, with June output 35% below nominal capacity.

Two caveats worth flagging for any downstream use: Russia classified crude production statistics in 2023 and petroleum product data in 2024, so all estimates are modeled rather than reported; and if a question resolves on mainstream reporting of the Ukrainian claim, 42.7%/43% is the operative number, whereas resolution on independent energy analysts lands nearer one-third to one-half.

sources.title: General Staff says Ukraine knocked out 42% of Russia's refining and cost industry $13.5 billion since August 2025
sources.snippet: On 4 July 2026 Ukraine's General Staff stated via Telegram that 42.74% of Russia's oil refining capacity has been idled by Ukrainian strikes. The figure sits between Honchar's 50% (30 June) and IEA/Reuters industry sources' 33–40% through June.

sources.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces Disable 43% of Russia's Total Oil Refining Capacity
sources.snippet: 42.7% (rounded to 43%) per the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, explicitly 'as of early July 2026'. $13.5 billion in industry losses since August 2025; 60+ storage reservoirs destroyed or critically damaged; 8 refineries struck in the past month.

sources.title: The Domestic and Global Impact of Ukraine's Attacks on Russian Oil Infrastructure (OIES Energy Comment, July 2026)
sources.snippet: In 2026 a total of 24 Russian refineries has been attacked by Ukrainian drones (out of the country's 34 plants), covering a capacity of 5.1 mb/d, equivalent to 81% of the country's total refining capacity... As of mid-June it was estimated that one third of Russia's refining capacity was offline at a single point in time. Total capacity table sums to 6,270 kbpd.

sources.title: Russia's Downstream Crisis Ripples Through Global Markets
sources.snippet: Published Thu, Jul 9, 2026. Nearly half of Russia's 6.6 million barrels per day of refining capacity has been knocked off line since late February. More than 3.1 million b/d of Russian refining capacity is currently down. Russian refining runs fell to 3.87 million b/d in June.

sources.title: Russian Refining: Drones Knock Out One-Third of Primary Capacity
sources.snippet: Published Thu, Jun 11, 2026. Nearly one-third, or 2.14 million b/d, of Russia's crude oil refining capacity is currently off line because of Ukrainian drone attacks. Refining runs in the first week of June plunged to below 4 million b/d, the lowest in 21 years.

sources.title: Ukrainian drones knock out up to 40% of Russia's oil refining capacity – FT
sources.snippet: Ukrainian drone strikes may have knocked out between 20% and 40% of Russia's oil refining capacity, per FT citing analyst estimates. In June Russia processed an average of 4.1 million barrels per day, 28% below the five-year average and 35% below nominal capacity.

sources.title: Russian oil refinery runs at 21-year lows after drone attacks
sources.snippet: Dated 7/14/2026. Kpler: as of mid-July, refinery downtime and attacked capacity stood at around 4.3 MMbpd, representing roughly 58% of Russia's refining capacity, with an estimated 1.5 MMbpd–2 MMbpd of processing capacity effectively offline. At least 25 refineries affected since August 2025.

sources.title: Ukraine burned half of Russia's oil refining, Ukrainian analyst says
sources.snippet: Mykhailo Honchar says half (50%) of Russia's primary oil refining capacity is now offline, published 30 June 2026 in ZN.UA. Higher than IEA and Reuters-cited industry estimates of 33–40% through June.

sources.title: Long-term impacts of Russian refinery outages (Wood Mackenzie, 05 August 2026)
sources.snippet: Russian refinery outages increased sharply in H1 2026 following sustained Ukrainian drone attacks. CDU outages reached 2.7 million b/d in July 2026, prompting revision of the short-term outage forecast from 1.0 million b/d to 2.0 million b/d.

sources.title: How Much Refining Capacity Has Russia Lost After the Omsk Refinery Was Struck?
sources.snippet: Reconciles ~40–45% (Ukrainian military framing) vs ~20–25% (independent market framing), noting they measure different things: disabled nameplate capacity vs output shortfall. Notes FT counted 194+ refinery strikes in H1 2026 and 8 of top 10 refineries hit.

sources.title: Russian Oil Refining Falls to 24-Year Low After Ukrainian Drone Strikes – Bloomberg
sources.snippet: Refineries processed an estimated 3.6 million barrels of crude per day in July, the lowest level since May 2002, per EA Analytics data cited by Bloomberg — roughly one-third below the seasonal norm of 5.3–5.6 million bpd for 2020–2025.

sources.title: Oil Refining in Russia Has Fallen to a Two-Decade Low
sources.snippet: 3.91 million barrels/day average Russian refinery processing in July 2026, lowest since March 2005, per EA Analytics (Energy Aspects) reported by Bloomberg on July 13, 2026. Down more than 1.4 million bpd vs July 2025. Russian crude output 8.928 million bpd in June.

sources.title: Ukrainian airstrikes disable over 30% of Russia's operating oil-refinery capacity, Financial Times reports
sources.snippet: FT satellite/thermal analysis with Frontelligence Insight: strikes disabled more than 30% of Russia's operating oil-refinery capacity and 45% of its nominal capacity, triggering the most severe fuel crisis since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

sources.title: Running on Empty: Russia's Fuel Crisis (CEPA, July 2, 2026)
sources.snippet: After the Kapotnya and TANECO strikes in mid-June, the loss of capacity may have reached 28% against prior years. Operating refineries producing ~85,000 tonnes of petrol per day against summer peak demand of ~110,000 tonnes. Eight of Russia's 10 largest refineries affected.

sources.title: Russian Oil Sector Battered but Not Broken by Ukrainian Air Attacks (Carnegie, Sergey Vakulenko)
sources.snippet: Ukrainian attacks on the Moscow refinery in Kapotnya and Tatneft's TANECO knocked out about 600,000 barrels a day in mid-June. If previously damaged refineries can't quickly restore output, Russia's loss of capacity might be 28 percent down on previous years.

sources.title: Ukrainian drones have knocked out nearly a third of Russia's oil refining capacity
sources.snippet: Ukrainian drone strikes have taken offline roughly 32% of oil refining in Russia, accounting for around 28% of the country's gasoline production, according to calculations by Novaya Gazeta Europe (21 May 2026).

sources.title: Russian Fuel Output Drops Up to 40% as Key Refineries Remain Offline
sources.snippet: Reported July 21 2026 by The Moscow Times citing Russian state media: companies restored slightly less than half of damaged capacity; facilities with combined capacity of 45 million tons of crude annually remain offline, 40 million tons/year restored.

sources.title: Ukraine's Strikes Have Disabled Nearly 43% of Russia's Oil Refining Capacity
sources.snippet: Ukraine's long-range strike campaign has disabled 42.74% of Russia's total oil refining capacity by design throughput, according to data released by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on July 4.

sources.title: Ukraine Disables Nearly 43% of Russia's Oil Refining Capacity — General Staff
sources.snippet: Ukraine's Defense Forces have disabled 42.74% of Russia's total oil refining capacity through a sustained campaign of long-range strikes; the campaign reached a new milestone at the beginning of July 2026.

sources.title: Ukraine claims it disabled over 40% of Russia's oil refining capacity as of early July
sources.snippet: Ukrainian General Staff claims Kyiv struck 8 Russian oil refineries over the past month; over 40% of Russia's oil refining capacity disabled as of early July.

key_facts: Ukraine's General Staff announced on 4 July 2026 that Ukrainian strikes had disabled 42.74% of Russia's total oil refining capacity by design throughput — the figure Kyiv Post explicitly datelines 'as of early July 2026'.

The same General Staff statement claimed 8 refineries struck in the prior month, 60+ storage tanks destroyed or critically damaged (58% products, 42% crude), and $13.5 billion in cumulative industry losses since August 2025.

There is no single agreed number: estimates circulating in early July 2026 ranged from ~20% to ~58%, because sources measure different things (cumulative capacity attacked vs. offline at a point in time vs. effectively offline vs. output shortfall).
Energy Intelligence (9 July 2026) reported 'nearly half' of Russia's 6.6 mb/d refining capacity knocked offline since late February, with more than 3.1 mb/d currently down (~47%).
The Financial Times (8–9 July 2026), citing analyst estimates, reported Ukrainian drones may have knocked out between 20% and 40% of Russia's oil refining capacity.
OIES (Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, July 2026) estimated that as of mid-June roughly one third of Russia's refining capacity was offline at a single point in time.

OIES found 24 of Russia's 34 refineries were attacked during 2026, covering 5.1 mb/d — 81% of national capacity — but noted not all were out of action simultaneously and several were hit more than once.

Kpler (14 July 2026) reported refinery downtime plus attacked capacity of ~4.3 mb/d, or roughly 58% of Russian refining capacity, but with only an estimated 1.5–2.0 mb/d of processing capacity effectively offline (~20–27%).
Wood Mackenzie recorded Russian CDU (crude distillation unit) outages reaching 2.7 million b/d in July 2026, prompting it to revise its short-term outage forecast from 1.0 to 2.0 million b/d.
Ukrainian energy analyst Mykhailo Honchar calculated on 30 June 2026 that half (50%) of Russia's primary refining capacity was offline — the high end of contemporaneous estimates.
IEA and Reuters-cited industry sources put the offline share at 33–40% through June 2026, bracketing the General Staff claim from below.
Russian refinery crude runs fell to 3.87 mb/d in June 2026 (Energy Intelligence), the lowest in more than 20 years; OIES/Kpler put June at 3.7 mb/d, the lowest in 21 years.
The Kyiv School of Economics (Boris Dodonov, via FT) reported June 2026 runs averaged 4.1 mb/d — 28% below the five-year average and 35% below nominal capacity.
Mid-July runs were ~3.80 mb/d (Kpler) and 3.91 mb/d (EA Analytics via Bloomberg, 13 July); full-July averaged 3.6 mb/d, the lowest since May 2002 (EA Analytics via Bloomberg, 3 August).
Total Russian refining capacity baselines differ by source: OIES uses 6.27 mb/d (6,270 kbpd across 33 listed plants), Energy Intelligence uses 6.6 mb/d, and Kpler's arithmetic implies ~7.4 mb/d.
June 2026 product output versus June 2025: gasoline −24%, jet fuel −23%, diesel −20% (OIES).
All 11 of Russia's largest refineries had been struck by early July 2026; 8 of the top 10 were affected. FT counted 194+ refinery strikes in H1 2026.
Russia's largest refinery, Omsk (428–450 kb/d, ~7–10% of national capacity), was struck for the first time on 6 July 2026 at roughly 2,500–3,000 km range, and halted operations.
The Moscow/Kapotnya refinery was hit twice (12 and 18 June 2026), disabling both crude-processing units; Reuters reported it would not return online until 2027.

The fuel crisis affected about 50 million Russians (~35% of the population); OIES reported 56 of Russia's 89 regions experiencing shortages, with ~50 regions imposing rationing by 25 June and Crimea under a state of emergency using electronic vouchers.
